cor.heading: Cost of sales
cor.text:
Cost of sales includes the cost of raw materials and components for manufacturing PV solar modules and BESS and system solutions. In addition, our cost of sales includes direct labor for the manufacturing of PV solar modules, BESS, system solutions and manufacturing overhead, such as engineering, equipment maintenance, quality and production control, and information technology. Our cost of sales also includes depreciation of manufacturing plant and equipment, facility-related expenses, environmental health and safety costs, and costs associated with shipping. These costs are offset by our generation of 45X Tax Credits.

Cost of sales decreased by $9.5 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026 and increased by $204.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same periods in 2025. The decrease for the three months ended September 30, 2026 is primarily due to lower sales volumes that correspondingly decreased net sales, partially offset by higher facilities-related costs during the period when compared to the same period in 2025. The primary increases for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 is a direct result of increased sales volumes that correspondingly increased net sales period over period along with higher facility-related expenses period over period.

ga.heading: Selling, general and administrative
ga.text:
Selling, general and administrative expenses primarily consist of personnel and personnel-related expenses for our sales, marketing and administrative personnel, commissions, royalty fees, costs for administrative offices, insurance, and outside professional services including legal, accounting, and other advisory services.

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased by $8.4 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, when compared to the same period in 2025, primarily due to higher legal and professional fees, higher personnel and share-based compensation expenses, partially offset by lower royalty expenses as a result of the Evervolt IP Acquisition and the reversal of previously recorded allowance for credit losses of $5.6 million with no comparable activity in 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, selling, general and administrative expenses increased by $25.8 million, when compared to the same period in 2025, which is primarily driven by higher personnel and share-based compensation, facilities expenses, legal and other professional service expenses and partially offset by lower fees and commissions payable to TUS under the offtake contract.

net sales.heading: Net sales
net sales.text:
Net sales consist of sales of PV solar modules, net of intangible asset amortization for customer contracts and sales and installation of battery energy storage systems and related services. We recognize sales for PV solar modules at a point in time following the transfer of control of the modules to the customer, which typically occurs upon shipment or delivery depending on the terms of the underlying contracts.

Total net sales decreased by $13.9 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026 and increased by $227.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same periods in 2025. Third-party sales of PV solar modules were nominal in 2026 because substantially all modules produced are sold to TUS under our offtake agreements, slightly offset by the third-party sales from T1 NRI's $6.7 million of energy storage systems sales during the three months ended September 30, 2026. The increase in related party sales during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily driven by increased production volume compared to the same periods in 2025. We began selling PV solar modules after our acquisition of all the shares of capital stock of Trina Solar (U.S.) Holding, Inc. and related subsidiaries on December 23, 2024 (the “Trina Business Combination”).

intro.text: In February 2025, we changed our corporate name from FREYR Battery, Inc. to T1 Energy Inc. We will not distinguish between our prior and current corporate name and will refer to our current corporate name throughout this Annual Report on Form 10-K. As such, unless expressly indicated or the context requires otherwise, the terms “T1,” “Company,” “we,” “us,” and “our” in this document refer to T1 Energy Inc., a Delaware corporation, and, where appropriate, its subsidiaries. T1 Energy Inc. is an energy solutions provider building an integrated U.S. solar supply chain for solar modules to invigorate the United States with scalable, reliable, and low-cost energy. We currently manufacture and sell photovoltaic (“PV”) solar modules in Texas and are constructing our PV solar cell fab in Texas.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

The G2_Austin project is capital intensive, and our ability to continue construction and procure and install equipment as planned depends on our ability to obtain and maintain adequate sources of funding on acceptable terms and at times required.
We also depend on third-party relationships in the development and construction of production equipment, which may subject us to the risk that such third parties do not fulfill their obligations.

Delays or difficulties during the G2_Austin ramp-up could materially impact revenue generation and debt service capacity, particularly during the early operational phase when the Company’s cash flows and ability to meet financial obligations depend on achieving planned production volumes.
Our growth strategy depends on the widespread adoption of solar power technology.
We depend on our suppliers to source materials and manufacture critical components for our products.
The suppliers rely on other suppliers to provide them with raw materials and sub-components that are critical to manufacturing the components of our tracker products.

Our business relies on information technology, and any failure, inadequacy, interruption, or security lapse affecting that technology, including any cybersecurity incidents, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

In addition, the IT systems we rely on may contain defects in design or manufacture, including bugs, security vulnerabilities, and other problems that could unexpectedly interfere with our security or operations.

Our success depends on our ability to attract and retain key personnel, including our executive officers, as well as qualified sales, marketing, manufacturing, plant operations, and support personnel.
Some of such employees’ ability to work in the United States depends on obtaining and maintaining necessary visas and work permits.

In addition, to the extent that we, or our key contractors, subcontractors or equipment suppliers supporting construction, installation, commissioning or ramp-up activities at G2_Austin rely on foreign national personnel, any inability by us or such parties, or any delay in obtaining required visas or work authorizations could disrupt these activities, delay our project timelines or increase costs.
Our ability to realize these benefits depends on our ability to satisfy applicable statutory requirements or regulatory guidance regarding Section 45X of the IRC.

The PFE Restrictions also prevent unrelated solar project developers from claiming credits under Sections 45Y and 48E of the IRC if the project relies too heavily on components manufactured by such foreign entities.
We also rely on a number of third parties in relation to the operation of our business, a number of which process data, including personal information, on our behalf.

The overall impact of trade laws on our business depends on multiple factors, including their duration, scope and potential expansion thereof, enforcement, retaliatory measures by impacted exporting countries, inflationary effects and broader macroeconomic responses, changes to consumer purchasing behavior, and the effectiveness of our responses in managing these impacts.
Our ability to refinance our indebtedness or preferred stock will depend on the capital markets and our financial condition at such time.

Because our decision to issue securities in any future offering and to enter into new loan agreements will depend on market conditions and other risk factors, many of which are beyond our control, we cannot predict or estimate the amount, timing or nature of our future offerings or borrowings.
As a result, capital appreciation, if any, of our shares of common stock would be your sole source of gain on an investment in such shares for the foreseeable future.

Our principal sources of liquidity are cash and cash equivalents, issuances of equity and debt securities, cash flows from operating activities and amounts received from government tax credits and incentives.

Our future liquidity requirements depend on many factors, including the timing and extent of the following: capital expenditures for construction of future facilities and purchase of related equipment; spending on other growth initiatives, including through joint ventures; spending to support revenue generating activities; and general economic conditions.

The failure of any key supplier to perform could disrupt our supply chain and impair our ability to deliver solar modules to customers in the required quality, quantities, and pricing, which could adversely affect our results of operations.
